title: PR #10 · An explainer in every PR

lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 10, which gives every issue's pull request an explainer page like this one.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request ten, which gives every issue's pull request an explainer page like this one.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
lines.say: Part one. What this pull request adds.

lines.caption: First, on the branch, the explainer skill writes the page from its template: three parts and a glossary.
The writer renders it locally with the same script CI uses, and looks at the picture before pushing.
Then the branch is pushed and the pull request opens. Every push reruns the workflow.
On the pull request, a new explainer job runs beside the build. First, it requires the page.
Then headless Chrome renders it in dark mode, 1200 pixels wide, as one full-page picture.
The picture is committed to the shots branch, in a folder for this pull request.
And it goes into one PR comment, which every later push updates in place.
lines.say: And it goes into one pull request comment, which every later push updates in place.

lines.caption: Why? The Files changed tab shows what changed, but not what it means, how it was checked, or what comes next.
And GitHub shows HTML in a private repo as source code, so CI posts a picture of the page instead.
The check looks at the files the PR adds or changes: a branch for issue 9 needs a page for issue 9.
lines.say: The check looks at the files the pull request adds or changes: a branch for issue nine needs a page for issue nine.

lines.caption: Chrome measures how tall the page is, then takes one screenshot exactly that tall, so nothing needs trimming.
The comment links the image by the commit that uploaded it, so a new push never shows an older picture.
The job finds its comment by a hidden marker, and replaces only the explainer section inside it.
That leaves room for issue 7, whose verify job will add its own section to the same comment.
lines.say: That leaves room for issue seven, whose verify job will add its own section to the same comment.

lines.caption: A branch for issue 9 that adds its page passes.
lines.say: A branch for issue nine that adds its page passes.

lines.caption: With no page, or with only another issue's page, it fails.
Branches not named after an issue, like a dependency bump, are exempt.
Only this job may write to the repo, and only to post the picture.
Only its last step gets the token, and the checkout keeps no credentials.
Pull requests from forks are skipped, check included, because their read-only token couldn't upload or comment.
There's also an optional video, made only on your machine, from a narration file committed with the page.
When the page changes, a status command names exactly the lines whose page text changed.
Kokoro, a speech model on the desktop, voices each line once and caches it.
lines.say: Kokoro, a speech model on the desktop, voices each line once, and caches it.

lines.caption: The page itself is the slides: a temporary copy shows one section at a time, with a highlight and a caption.
And ffmpeg joins the frames and the voice into an mp4 with chapters. The video isn't committed.
In all, the PR adds the skill, the CI script and job, a short CLAUDE.md, and this page with its narration.
lines.say: In all, the pull request adds the skill, the CI script and job, a short CLAUDE.md, and this page with its narration.

lines.caption: Part 2. How it was built and verified.
lines.say: Part two. How it was built and verified.

lines.caption: The template comes from PR 8's hand-made page, with ids and highlight keys added for the video.
lines.say: The template comes from pull request eight's hand-made page, with section names and highlight keys added for the video.

lines.caption: The video script grew out of PR 8's one-off script, with the page itself replacing its hand-made slides.
lines.say: The video script grew out of pull request eight's one-off script, with the page itself replacing its hand-made slides.

lines.caption: And the CI script follows the release scripts' style, including a dry-run mode.
A fresh agent, given only the skill, wrote PR 8's page. Its structure matched the hand-made one, and 10 gaps it hit were fixed in the skill.
lines.say: A fresh agent, given only the skill, wrote pull request eight's page. Its structure matched the hand-made one, and ten gaps it hit were fixed in the skill.

lines.caption: The required check ran on five local branches: one passed, three failed and one was exempt, as intended.
Adding a page to the failing branch made it pass.
A dry run of the whole script rendered this page and printed the comment, without uploading anything.
Updating a comment kept the other section in it, in both cases tried.
And a page too wide for a phone got a warning.
The first real run on GitHub posted this page as an image, in a comment of its own.
A second push, updating that same comment, hadn't run yet when this was written.
This video's picture and sound match to within a frame, and it has five chapters.
After one sentence on the page changed, only its one narration line was rewritten and voiced again.
And at a sampled line, the caption changes in the pause before the voice starts.
Not checked: the voice, by ear. Pronunciation was checked from Kokoro's phonemes instead.
Also not run: a pull request from a fork, and two pull requests uploading at the same moment.
A code review before the first push found 10 issues. 8 are fixed here.
lines.say: A code review before the first push found ten issues. Eight are fixed here.

lines.caption: They were edge cases in both scripts: stale files, missing images, unusual paths and unescaped text.
The other 2 were kept as decided in issue 9, such as fork PRs skipping the check.
lines.say: The other two were kept as decided in issue nine, such as pull requests from forks skipping the check.

lines.caption: After the merge, the first cloud session will show whether it follows the new CLAUDE.md.
And the next issue PR will be the first to get its own folder and comment.
lines.say: And the next issue's pull request will be the first to get its own folder and comment.

lines.caption: Part 3. What comes later: issue 7, then the feature PRs.
lines.say: Part three. What comes later: issue seven, then the feature pull requests.

lines.caption: This PR builds the skill, the explainer job, and one proof comment per pull request.
lines.say: This pull request builds the skill, the explainer job, and one proof comment per pull request.

lines.caption: Issue 7's verify job will run Thunar on a virtual screen, and add its results to the same comment.
lines.say: Issue seven's verify job will run Thunar on a virtual screen, and add its results to the same comment.

lines.caption: Its cloud agents read CLAUDE.md, and open pull requests with an explainer written with this skill.
Then each feature PR, issues 3 to 6, arrives with its page, its picture and CI's proof.
lines.say: Then each feature pull request, issues three to six, arrives with its page, its picture, and C I's proof.

lines.caption: The trial run is issue 3, double-click to go to the parent folder, built end to end by a cloud session.
lines.say: The trial run is issue three, double-click to go to the parent folder, built end to end by a cloud session.

lines.caption: And issue 2's auto-deploy gets a page like this one too.
lines.say: And issue two's auto-deploy gets a page like this one too.

lines.caption: That's the whole flow: a skill writes the page, CI requires it and shows it, and a video is one command away.
